docs.title: dev-aliases
docs.text:
One-click installer for Terraform and Git aliases on Windows — works in both CMD and PowerShell.

If you work with Terraform and Git daily, you already know the pain of typing long repetitive commands. dev-aliases installs short, memorable shortcuts so you can focus on building — not typing.

docs.title: What's Included
docs.text:
Tool Total Aliases Terraform 10 tf tfi tfp tfa tfd tfv tff tfo tfs tfws Git 18 g gs ga gc gp gl gb gco gd glog gst gstp grs grss gm grb grt gcl

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
Before: 

terraform apply --auto-approve
git log --oneline
git restore --staged .

After:

glog
grss .

docs.title: Alias Reference
docs.text: Complete reference for all installed aliases with descriptions and workflow examples.

docs.title: Terraform
docs.text: Alias Command Description tf terraform Base Terraform command tfi terraform init Initialize a working directory and download providers tfp terraform plan Preview what changes will be applied tfa terraform apply --auto-approve Apply changes without a confirmation prompt tfd terraform destroy --auto-approve Destroy all resources without a confirmation prompt tfv terraform validate Check configuration files for syntax errors tff terraform fmt Auto-format .tf files to canonical style tfo terraform output Display output values defined in the configuration tfs terraform show Inspect the current state or a saved plan file tfws terraform workspace List, create, or switch Terraform workspaces

docs.title: Terraform Workflows
docs.text:
# Standard deploy flow
tfi                    # terraform init
tfv                    # terraform validate
tfp                    # terraform plan
tfa                    # terraform apply --auto-approve

# Inspect state
tfs                    # terraform show
tfo                    # terraform output

# Workspace management
tfws list              # list all workspaces
tfws new staging       # create a new workspace
tfws select staging    # switch to a workspace

# Teardown
tfd                    # terraform destroy --auto-approve

docs.title: Git
docs.text: Alias Command Description g git Base Git command gs git status Show the state of the working tree and staging area ga git add Stage changes for the next commit gc git commit Record staged changes with a message gp git push Push local commits to the remote repository gl git pull Fetch and integrate changes from the remote gb git branch List, create, rename, or delete branches gco git checkout Switch branches or restore working tree files gd git diff Show differences between working tree and index glog git log --oneline Display a compact, one-line commit history gst git stash Temporarily save uncommitted changes gstp git stash pop Re-apply the most recently stashed changes grs git restore Discard changes in the working directory grss git restore --staged Remove files from the staging area gm git merge Merge a branch into the currently active branch grb git rebase Reapply commits on top of another base branch grt git remote -v List all configured remote repositories with URLs gcl git clone Clone a remote repository to your local machine

docs.title: Git Workflows
docs.text:
# Daily commit flow
gs                           # git status
ga .                         # git add .
gc -m "feat: add feature"    # git commit -m "..."
gp                           # git push

# Feature branch workflow
gb feature/my-feature        # create branch
gco feature/my-feature       # switch to branch
ga . && gc -m "feat: done"
gp

# Stash and switch context
gst                          # stash current work
gco main && gl               # switch to main and pull
gco feature/my-feature
gstp                         # restore stashed work

# Undo mistakes
grs file.txt                 # discard changes in file
grss file.txt                # unstage a staged file
glog                         # review commit history

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Thank you for your interest in contributing! All skill levels are welcome.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
1. Fork this repository
  2. Clone your fork: 
    gcl https://github.com/your-username/install-dev-aliases.git
  3. Create a new branch: 
    gco -b feat/add-docker-aliases

docs.title: Adding a New Alias Group
docs.text: Adding a new tool requires changes in three places:

docs.title: 1. scripts/install.cmd
docs.text:
Add a new block in the Creating CMD aliases section:

:: ---------- Docker ----------
(echo @echo off & echo docker %%*)           > "%ALIAS_DIR%\d.cmd"
(echo @echo off & echo docker ps %%*)        > "%ALIAS_DIR%\dps.cmd"
(echo @echo off & echo docker logs -f %%*)   > "%ALIAS_DIR%\dlogs.cmd"

docs.title: 2. scripts/install.ps1
docs.text:
Add to the $cmdAliases hashtable:

"d.cmd"     = "docker %*"
"dps.cmd"   = "docker ps %*"
"dlogs.cmd" = "docker logs -f %*"

Add matching functions to the $block here-string:

# Docker
function d       { docker @args }
function dps     { docker ps @args }
function dlogs   { docker logs -f @args }

docs.title: 3. Update the docs
docs.text:
• Add a new table in docs/aliases-reference.md
  • Update the summary table in docs/index.md
  • Update README.md

docs.title: Submitting a Pull Request
docs.text:
ga .
gc -m "feat: add Docker aliases"
gp origin feat/add-docker-aliases

Then open a PR on GitHub with:

  • A clear title like feat: add Docker aliases
  • A short description of what was added and why it's useful
  • Confirmation that you tested in both CMD and PowerShell

docs.title: Guidelines
docs.text:
Keep these in mind

  • Keep alias names short (2–5 characters)
  • Only include commands commonly used in DevOps workflows
  • Avoid aliases that conflict with existing system commands
  • Test in both CMD and PowerShell before submitting

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Both installers do the same thing — pick whichever shell you prefer.

docs.title: What the Installer Does
docs.text:
• Creates .cmd wrapper files in %USERPROFILE%\bin for CMD support
  • Injects shell functions into your PowerShell $PROFILE for PS support
  • Automatically adds %USERPROFILE%\bin to your User PATH
  • Safe to re-run — updates existing aliases without duplicates

docs.title: Option 1 — CMD
docs.text:
Double-click install.cmd or run it in any terminal:

scripts\install.cmd

docs.title: Option 2 — PowerShell
docs.text:
# One-time setup (if not already done)
Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned

# Run the installer
.\scripts\install.ps1

Restart Your Terminal

After installation, close and reopen your terminal for aliases to take effect.

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text:
After restarting your terminal, test a few aliases:

tf --version      # should run: terraform --version
gs                # should run: git status
glog              # should run: git log --oneline
